fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Front Entry Area; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach the front of the residence.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive that overhang or narrow the travel path.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the walls or roofline of the main residence.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the walls or roofline of the detached structure.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between them on foot.
• Mark or unlock any gate controlling access to the rear of the property so responders can locate and open it quickly.
• Trim vegetation along the perimeter fencing line that would block or slow responder movement around the property.
• Keep the walkway from the driveway to the front entry clear of planters, furniture, or overgrown landscaping.
• Identify and communicate to household members an alternate exit route in the event the single access drive is blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure so branches do not extend close to the roofline or walls.
• Clear any dead leaves, branches, or plant debris that has collected against the base of the structure.
• Keep the single access route free of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along both sides.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate and navigate quickly.
• Cut back vegetation along the rear of the property to open a path wide enough for a person to move around the back of the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings near outbuildings or other improvements so they do not connect directly to the main structure.
• Keep the open green space mowed or grazed short to maintain the existing separation between vegetation and the structure.
